reason: Both conversations unplugged first, used the drum-turn test, respected the back-injury limit and escalated sensibly to an engineer, and neither checked levelling or the condensate pump. Conversation 2 reasoned better: it used the drum roughness as a discriminator and kept both worn rollers and the idler pulley in play (matching the genuine uncertainty), and correctly told the owner it is safe to keep using the dryer as this is not urgent. Conversation 1 locked onto 'jockey pulley or idler wheel' despite roughness pointing at rollers, asked a non-tooled owner to remove the top panel, and ended with needless 'keep it unplugged' advice, though it did usefully try to localise the noise. Conversation 2's 'almost certainly' overstates confidence and its dead-end model-number panel was clumsy, which keeps the margin slight.
